projects.title: Projects

pulsar.short: Neutron, the scripting language of the Pulsar game engine: I built its whole pipeline, from lexer to interpreter, in Rust.
pulsar.full: Pulsar is the game engine built for our Epitech final-year project. I was in charge of Neutron, its scripting language, written in Rust: lexical analysis, parser and syntax tree, semantic analysis with static typing, scopes and symbol table, then the interpreter. Every stage of the pipeline is covered by unit and integration tests.
highlights: Lexer, parser and abstract syntax tree (AST)
Semantic analysis: static typing, scopes, symbol table
Language interpreter
Unit and integration tests at every stage

projects.subtitle: An app in production, school projects and personal quantum computing projects.

kiwanis.short: Mobile and web app for Kiwanis club members, published on Google Play.
kiwanis.full: Mon Kiwanis brings a club's life into a single app: event calendar with attendance tracking, polls, news feed, fundraising campaign tracking and a member directory. I designed and built it end to end, from the TypeScript mobile app with Expo to the API, then published it on Google Play and as a web app.
highlights: Designed and built end to end
Events and attendance, polls, social feed, directory
Fundraising campaign tracking
Published on Google Play and on the web

qsim.short: Quantum circuit simulator written from scratch in Python, checked against Qiskit and within 1.3x of qiskit-aer.
qsim.full: qsim simulates quantum circuits with two backends: a state vector, where gates are applied without ever building a huge matrix, and a density matrix that models noise (depolarizing, damping, T1/T2 relaxation, readout errors). The Numba kernels update the state in place, in parallel, and stay within 1.2-1.3x of qiskit-aer, the reference C++ simulator. It reads and writes OpenQASM 2 and supports mid-circuit measurement. 108 tests compare every backend to Qiskit on random circuits.
highlights: State-vector and density-matrix backends with noise models
Parallel Numba kernels, within 1.2-1.3x of qiskit-aer
OpenQASM 2 parser and exporter, mid-circuit measurement
108 cross-validation tests against Qiskit, CI

qalgo.short: Benchmark of textbook quantum algorithms on noise models of three IBM processors: what is left of the ideal result?
qalgo.full: This project runs Deutsch-Jozsa, Bernstein-Vazirani, Grover, phase estimation and GHZ state preparation at increasing sizes, on an ideal simulator and then with the noise, native gates and connectivity of three IBM processors (Sherbrooke, Torino, Fez). It measures the drift from the ideal output and shows that fidelity depends mostly on the number of two-qubit gates after compilation, with an effective error per gate fitted for each processor. A script runs the same suite on real IBM hardware.
highlights: 5 algorithms on 3 simulated IBM processors
Fidelity modeled from the two-qubit gate count
Impact of transpiler settings and qubit placement
Results and plots documented in the README

zappy.short: Networked game where AI teams compete on a toroidal map. I built the AI client and the network side of the graphical interface.
zappy.full: Zappy is made of three programs: a server in C, a 3D graphical interface in C++ and autonomous AI clients. The AIs gather resources and perform rituals to level up; the first team to get six players to level 8 wins. In the team of four, I wrote the Python AI client (protocol, strategy, team coordination through messages) and the network side of the graphical interface.
highlights: My part: autonomous AI client in Python
Player coordination through messages for the rituals
Network side of the graphical interface
Team project of four

raytracer.short: Ray tracing renderer in C++. Started by a team of three at Epitech, where I wrote the scene parser and object factory, then finished on my own.
raytracer.full: The raytracer renders an image from a scene file (libconfig++): spheres, planes, cylinders and cones, translations and rotations, ambient, directional and point lights, Phong shading, shadows and reflections. Rendering is spread across every CPU core and smoothed with supersampling. The project was started by a team of three in 2023 (I wrote the scene parser and object factory), then I picked it up and finished it on my own.
highlights: Scene parser and object factory
Spheres, planes, cylinders, cones, transformations
Phong shading, shadows and reflections
Multithreaded rendering with antialiasing
